segment:
Welcome

Mara smiled and went in, approaching the couch from the far end to avoid closing it off. “Hi. Mara.” She put down her tote bag and sat in the single chair opposite him.
He was gazing at her, not just at her eyes but her whole face. Mara felt something like a blush under his gaze, and a quick sense of being seen. There was a hint of a smile or some kind of lift, as if her presence or her movement had given him a little joy.
“Jonah.” His voice was soft, with the slight lilt of the south.

“You live here?” she asked, sitting forward.

He tilted his head again, and this time the gesture seemed to have some significance—was it a question? She watched his eyes as she said, “I’m the new postdoc.”

Still he only gazed at her.

Mara tried to relax into the chair. After a pause, she said, “You were just here yesterday, right? When I came for the interview.”

“Yes.”

“I saw your picture on the wall yesterday. You won some kind of award?”

He said something in a tone too low for her to make out, as if he’d heard himself too much or felt awkward about hearing.

“The award,” she repeated.

This time his mouth closed without speaking. There was something more complicated than shyness in his manner, and some hint of an exchange between them, although she wasn’t sure if the meaning was real or imaginary.

Mara looked away, giving herself a little more time. She watched his hands for a moment, how they twined around each other, one thumb rubbing the other thumb.
text:
When Mara walked into the common room at six fifteen, someone was already there. Someone younger, it seemed.
She couldn’t make out the face behind the blond hair. But the body was fine enough, leaning back on the couch with bare legs crossed and arms flung in opposite directions, one palm pressing the padded wall and the other wrist resting on the low table beside him.
She stood stock-still by the doorway for a moment, aware of her breath and of his awareness that she was here. He stirred and tilted his head; a face turned toward her, expressionless.

segment:
“Hi,” Mara said softly, then tried to remember what she’d been told to say. “Um, it’s my first day at Fulcrum. I’m Mara.”
She held up the small card in her hand. Her name was there, and the word TRAINEE.
His eyes drifted toward the card as he took a moment to reply.
“I’m Adrian.” He put his right arm down again. “Welcome.”
The right hand spread out over the surface of the low table; the fingers flexed lightly. Mara felt slightly exposed, though he’d already been here when she arrived. She tried not to think about how her own body was positioned, only to note how Adrian was occupying space. She stepped forward slowly.
“I don’t know quite what to do next,” Mara said. “Should I be sitting down or—”
“Wait.”
His tone was low and even, but somehow the word had an edge to it that she couldn’t account for. Mara stopped midstep, holding perfectly still. She looked at her feet and wondered if she was doing what he wanted her to do. There was a slight ripple in the air; one of the corners of his mouth seemed to turn upward. His hand shifted on the table surface, then turned over as if he was tapping something invisible just out of his reach.
Mara took her eyes off her feet, lifted them up the length of his arm toward his face. He was still watching her. She tried not to imagine what she might be seeing in his expression, what he might be seeing in hers. He cleared his throat.
“Can you come sit down here?”
